38.11: And Ebed-Melech takes the men with him, and enters the house of the king, to the place of the treasury, and takes from there worn-out clouts, and worn-out rags, and sends them to Jeremiah to the pit by cords.
38.12: And Ebed-Melech the Cushite says to Jeremiah, `Put, I pray you, the worn-out clouts and rags under your arm-holes, at the place of the cords,' and Jeremiah does so,
38.13: and they draw out Jeremiah with cords, and bring him up out of the pit, and Jeremiah dwells in the court of the prison.
38.14: And the king Zedekiah sends, and takes Jeremiah the prophet to him, to the third entrance that is in the house of Jehovah, and the king says to Jeremiah, `I am asking you a thing, do not hide from me anything.'
38.15: And Jeremiah says to Zedekiah, `When I declare to you, do you not surely put me to death? and when I counsel you, you do not hearken to me.'
38.16: And the king Zedekiah swears to Jeremiah in secret, saying, `Jehovah lives, He who made for us this soul, I do not put you to death, nor give you to the hand of these men who are seeking your soul.'
38.17: And Jeremiah says to Zedekiah, `Thus said Jehovah, God of Hosts, God of Israel: If you do certainly go forth to the heads of the king of Babylon, then has your soul lived, and this city is not burned with fire, yes, you have lived, you and your house.
38.18: And if you do not go forth to the heads of the king of Babylon, then has this city been given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they have burnt it with fire, and you do not escape from their hand.'
38.19: And the king Zedekiah says to Jeremiah, `I am fearing the Jews who have fallen to the Chaldeans, lest they give me into their hand, and they have insulted me.'
38.20: And Jeremiah says, `They do not give you up; hearken, I pray you, to the voice of Jehovah, to that which I am speaking to you, and it is well for you, and your soul does live.
38.21: `And if you are refusing to go forth, this is the thing that Jehovah has shown me:
38.22: That, indeed, all the women who have been left in the house of the king of Judah are brought forth to the heads of the king of Babylon, and indeed, they are saying: Persuaded you, and prevailed against you, Have your allies, Sunk into mire have your feet, They have been turned backward.
38.23: `And all your wives, and your sons, are brought forth to the Chaldeans, and you do not escape from their hand, for by the hand of the king of Babylon you are caught, and this city is burnt with fire.'
38.24: And Zedekiah says to Jeremiah, `Let no man know of these words, and you do not die;
38.25: and when the heads hear that I have spoken with you, and they have come in to you, and have said to you, Declare to us, we pray you, what you did speak to the king, do not hide it from us, and we do not put you to death, and what the king spoke to you,
38.26: then you have said to them, I am causing my supplication to fall before the king, not to cause me to return to the house of Jonathan, to die there.'
38.27: And all the heads come in to Jeremiah, and ask him, and he declares to them according to all these words that the king commanded, and they keep silent from him, for the matter was not heard;
38.28: and Jeremiah dwells in the court of the prison till the day that Jerusalem has been captured, and he was there when Jerusalem was captured.

39.1: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, come has Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his force to Jerusalem, and they lay siege against it;
39.2: in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, in the ninth of the month, has the city been broken up;
39.3: and come in do all the heads of the king of Babylon, and they sit at the middle gate, Nergal-Sharezer, Samgar-Nebo, Sarsechim, chief of the eunuchs, Nergal-Sharezer, chief of the Mages, and all the rest of the heads of the king of Babylon.
39.4: And it comes to pass, when Zedekiah king of Judah, and all the men of war, have seen them, that they flee and go forth by night from the city, the way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls, and he goes forth the way of the plain.
39.5: And the forces of the Chaldeans pursue after them, and overtake Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and they take him, and bring him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, to Riblah, in the land of Hamath, and he speaks with him--judgments.
39.6: And the king of Babylon slaughters the sons of Zedekiah, in Riblah, before his eyes, yes, all the freemen of Judah has the king of Babylon slaughtered.
39.7: And the eyes of Zedekiah he has blinded, and he binds him with brazen fetters, to bring him in to Babylon.
39.8: And the house of the king, and the house of the people, have the Chaldeans burnt with fire, and the walls of Jerusalem they have broken down.
39.9: And the remnant of the people who are left in the city, and those falling who have fallen to him, and the remnant of the people who are left, has Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, removed to Babylon.
39.10: And of the poor people, who have nothing, has Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, left in the land of Judah, and he gives to them vineyards and fields on the same day.
39.11: And Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon gives a charge concerning Jeremiah, by the hand of Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, saying,
39.12: `Take him, and place your eyes upon him, and do no evil thing to him, but as he speaks to you, so do with him.'
39.13: And Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners sends, and Nebushazban, chief of the eunuchs, and Nergal-Sharezer, chief of the Mages, and all the chiefs of the king of Babylon;
39.14: yes, they send and take Jeremiah out of the court of the prison, and give him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, to carry him home, and he dwells in the midst of the people.
39.15: And to Jeremiah has a word of Jehovah been--in his being detained in the court of the prison--saying:
39.16: `Go, and you have spoken to Ebed-Melech the Cushite, saying: Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Indeed, I am bringing in My words to this city for evil, and not for good, and they have been before you in that day.
39.17: And I have delivered you in that day--an affirmation of Jehovah--and you are not given into the hand of the men of whose face you are afraid,
39.18: for I do certainly deliver you, and by sword you fall not, and your life has been to you for a spoil, for you have trusted in Me--an affirmation of Jehovah.'

40.1: The word that has been to Jeremiah from Jehovah, after Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, has sent him from Ramah, in his taking him--and he a prisoner in chains--in the midst of all the removal of Jerusalem and of Judah, who are removed to Babylon.
40.2: And the chief of the executioners takes Jeremiah, and says to him, `Jehovah your God has spoken this evil concerning this place,
40.3: and Jehovah brings it in, and does as He spoke, because you have sinned against Jehovah, and have not hearkened to His voice, even this thing has been to you.
40.4: `And now, indeed, I have loosed you to-day from the chains that are on your hand; if good in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, come, and I keep my eye upon you: and if evil in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, forbear; see, all the land is before you, where it be good, and where it be right in your eyes to go--go.' --
40.5: and while he does not reply--`Or turn back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and dwell with him in the midst of the people, or wherever it is right in your eyes to go--go.' And the chief of the executioners gives to him for the way, and a gift, and sends him away,
40.6: and Jeremiah comes in to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, to Mizpah, and dwells with him, in the midst of the people who are left in the land.
40.7: And all the heads of the forces that are in the field hear, they and their men, that the king of Babylon has appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and that he has charged him with men, and women, and infants, and of the poor of the land, of those who have not been removed to Babylon;
40.8: and they come in to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maachathite, they and their men.
40.9: And swear to them does Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and to their men, saying, `Be not afraid of serving the Chaldeans, abide in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it is well for you;
40.10: and I, indeed, I am dwelling in Mizpah, to stand before the Chaldeans who are come in to us, and you, gather you wine, and summer fruit, and oil, and put in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken.'
40.11: And also all the Jews who are in Moab, and among the sons of Ammon, and in Edom, and who are in all the lands, have heard that the king of Babylon has given a remnant to Judah, and that he has appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan,
40.12: and all the Jews from all the places where they have been driven, turn back and enter the land of Judah, to Gedaliah, to Mizpah, and they gather wine and summer fruit--very much.
40.13: And Johanan son of Kareah, and all the heads of the forces that are in the field, have come in to Gedaliah to Mizpah,
40.14: and they say to him, `Do you really know that Baalis king of the sons of Ammon has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to smite your soul?' And Gedaliah son of Ahikam has not given to them credence.
40.15: And Johanan son of Kareah has spoken to Gedaliah in secret, in Mizpah, saying, `Let me go, I pray you, and I smite Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one does know; why does he smite your soul? and scattered have been all Judah who are gathered to you, and perished has the remnant of Judah.'
40.16: And Gedaliah son of Ahikam says to Johanan son of Kareah, `You do not do this thing, for falsehood you are speaking concerning Ishmael.'

41.1: And it comes to pass, in the seventh month, come has Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the seed royal, and of the chiefs of the king, and ten men with him, to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, to Mizpah, and they eat there bread together in Mizpah.
41.2: And Ishmael son of Nethaniah rises, and the ten men who have been with him, and they smite Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword, and he puts him to death whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the land.
41.3: And all the Jews who have been with him, with Gedaliah, in Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who have been found there--the men of war--has Ishmael smitten.
41.4: And it comes to pass, on the second day of the putting of Gedaliah to death, (and no one has known,)
41.5: that men come in from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria--eighty men--with shaven beards, and rent garments, and cutting themselves, and an offering and frankincense in their hand, to bring in to the house of Jehovah.
41.6: And Ishmael son of Nethaniah goes forth to meet them, from Mizpah, going on and weeping, and it comes to pass, at meeting them, that he says to them, `Come in to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.'
41.7: And it comes to pass, at their coming in to the midst of the city, that Ishmael son of Nethaniah does slaughter them, at the midst of the pit, he and the men who are with him.
41.8: And ten men have been found among them, and they say to Ishmael, `Do not put us to death, for we have things hidden in the field--wheat, and barley, and oil, and honey.' And he forbears, and has not put them to death in the midst of their brethren.
41.9: And the pit where Ishmael has cast all the carcases of the men whom he has smitten along with Gedaliah, is that which the king Asa made because of Baasha king of Israel--it has Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled with the pierced.
41.10: And Ishmael takes captive all the remnant of the people who are in Mizpah, the daughters of the king, and all the people who are left in Mizpah, whom Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, has committed to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and Ishmael son of Nethaniah takes them captive, and goes to pass over to the sons of Ammon.
41.11: And hear does Johanan son of Kareah, and all the heads of the forces that are with him, of all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah has done,
41.12: and they take all the men, and go to fight with Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they find him at the great waters that are in Gibeon.
41.13: And it comes to pass, when all the people who are with Ishmael see Johanan son of Kareah, and all the heads of the forces who are with him, that they rejoice.
41.14: And all the people whom Ishmael has taken captive from Mizpah turn round, yes, they turn back, and go to Johanan son of Kareah.
41.15: And Ishmael son of Nethaniah has escaped, with eight men, from the presence of Johanan, and he goes to the sons of Ammon.
41.16: And Johanan son of Kareah, and all the heads of the forces who are with him, take all the remnant of the people whom he has brought back from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah--after he had smitten Gedaliah son of Ahikam--mighty ones, men of war, and women, and infants, and eunuchs, whom he had brought back from Gibeon,
41.17: and they go and abide in the habitations of Chimham, that are near Beth-Lehem, to go to enter Egypt,
41.18: from the presence of the Chaldeans, for they have been afraid of them, for Ishmael son of Nethaniah had smitten Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.

42.1: And they come nigh--all the heads of the forces, and Johanan son of Kareah, and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even to the greatest--
42.2: and they say to Jeremiah the prophet, `Let, we pray you, our supplication fall before you, and pray for us to Jehovah your God, for all this remnant; for we have been left a few out of many, as your eyes do see us;
42.3: and Jehovah your God does declare to us the way in which we walk, and the thing that we do.'
42.4: And Jeremiah the prophet says to them, `I have heard: indeed, I am praying to Jehovah your God according to your words, and it has come to pass, the whole word that Jehovah answers you, I declare to you--I do not withhold from you a word.'
42.5: And they have said to Jeremiah, `Jehovah is against us for a witness true and faithful, if--according to all the word with which Jehovah your God does send you to us--we do not so.
42.6: Whether good or evil, to the voice of Jehovah our God, to whom we are sending you, we do hearken; because it is good for us when we hearken to the voice of Jehovah our God.'
42.7: And it comes to pass, at the end of ten days, that there is a word of Jehovah to Jeremiah,
42.8: and he calls to Johanan son of Kareah, and to all the heads of the forces that are with him, and to all the people, from the least even to the greatest,
42.9: and he says to them, `Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, to whom you sent me, to cause your supplication to fall before Him:
42.10: `If you do certainly dwell in this land, then I have builded you up, and I throw not down; and I have planted you, and I pluck not up; for I have repented concerning the evil that I have done to you.
42.11: Be not afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you are afraid of; be not afraid of him--an affirmation of Jehovah--for with you am I, to save you, and to deliver you from his hand.
42.12: And I give to you mercies, and he has pitied you, and caused you to turn back to your own ground.
42.13: `And if you are saying, We do not dwell in this land--not to hearken to the voice of Jehovah your God,
42.14: saying, No; but the land of Egypt we enter, that we see no war, and the sound of a trumpet do not hear, and for bread be not hungry; and there do we dwell.
42.15: And now, therefore, hear you a word of Jehovah, O remnant of Judah: Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: If you really set your faces to enter Egypt, and have gone in to sojourn there,
42.16: then it has come to pass, the sword that you are afraid of, does there overtake you, in the land of Egypt; and the hunger, because of which you are sorrowful, does there cleave after you in Egypt, and there you die.
42.17: `Thus are all the men who have set their faces to enter Egypt to sojourn there; they die--by sword, by hunger, and by pestilence, and there is not to them a remnant and an escaped one, because of the evil that I am bringing in upon them;
42.18: for thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: As poured out has been My anger and My fury on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so poured out is My fury upon you in your entering Egypt, and you have been for an execration, and for an astonishment, and for a reviling, and for a reproach, and you do not see any more this place.
42.19: `Jehovah has spoken against you, O remnant of Judah, do not enter Egypt: know certainly that I have testified against you to-day;
42.20: for you have showed yourselves perverse in your souls, for you sent me to Jehovah your God, saying, Pray for us to Jehovah our God, and according to all that Jehovah our God says, so declare to us, and we have done it;
42.21: and I declare to you to-day, and you have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah your God, and to anything with which He has sent me to you.
42.22: And now, know you certainly that by sword, by famine, and by pestilence you die, in the place that you have desired to go in to sojourn there.'

43.1: And it comes to pass, when Jeremiah does finish to speak to all the people all the words of Jehovah their God, with which Jehovah their God has sent him to them--all these words--
43.2: that Azariah son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan son of Kareah, and all the proud men, speak to Jeremiah, saying, `Falsehood you are speaking; Jehovah our God has not sent you to say, Do not enter Egypt to sojourn there;
43.3: for Baruch son of Neriah is moving you against us, in order to give us up into the hand of the Chaldeans, to put us to death, and to remove us to Babylon.'
43.4: And Johanan son of Kareah, and all the heads of the forces, and all the people, have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, to dwell in the land of Judah;
43.5: and Johanan son of Kareah, and all the heads of the forces, take all the remnant of Judah who have turned from all the nations where they were driven to sojourn in the land of Judah,
43.6: the men, and the women, and the infant, and the daughters of the king, and every person that Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch son of Neriah,
43.7: and they enter the land of Egypt, for they have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, and they enter to Tahpanhes.
43.8: And there is a word of Jehovah to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
43.9: `Take in your hand great stones, and you have hidden them, in the clay, in the brick-kiln, that is at the opening of the house of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes, before the eyes of the men of Judah,
43.10: and you have said to them: Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: `Indeed, I am sending, and I have taken Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, My servant, and I have set his throne above these stones that I have hid, and he has stretched out his pavilion over them,
43.11: and he has come, and smitten the land of Egypt--those who are for death to death, and those who are for captivity to captivity, and those who are for the sword to the sword.
43.12: And I have kindled a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, and it has burned them, and he has taken them captive, and covered himself with the land of Egypt, as cover himself does the shepherd with his garment, and he has gone forth from there in peace;
43.13: and he has broken the standing pillars of the house of the sun, that is in the land of Egypt, and the houses of the gods of Egypt he does burn with fire.'

44.1: The word that has been to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews who are dwelling in the land of Egypt--who are dwelling in Migdol, and in Tahpanhes, and in Noph, and in the land of Pathros--saying,
44.2: `Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: You--you have seen all the evil that I have brought in on Jerusalem, and on all the cities of Judah, and indeed, they are a waste this day, and there is none dwelling in them,
44.3: because of their wickedness that they have done, by provoking Me to anger, by going to make perfume, by serving other gods, that they knew not, they, you, and your fathers.
44.4: `And I send to you all my servants, the prophets, rising early and sending, saying: I pray you, do not this abomination that I have hated--
44.5: and they have not hearkened nor inclined their ear, to turn back from their wickedness, not to make perfume to other gods,
44.6: and poured out is My fury, and My anger, and it burns in cities of Judah, and in streets of Jerusalem, and they are for a waste, for a desolation, as at this day.
44.7: `And, now, thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Why are you doing great evil to your own souls, to cut off to you man and woman, infant and suckling, from the midst of Judah, so as not to leave to you a remnant:
44.8: by provoking Me to anger by the works of your hands, by making perfume to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you are going in to sojourn, so as to cut yourselves off, and so as to your being for a reviling and for a reproach among all nations of the earth?
44.9: `Have you forgotten the wickedness of your fathers, and the wickedness of the kings of Judah, and the wickedness of their wives, and your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives, that they have done in the land of Judah, and in streets of Jerusalem?
44.10: They have not been humbled to this day, nor have they been afraid, nor have they walked in My law, and in My statutes, that I have set before you and before your fathers.
44.11: `Therefore, thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Indeed, I am setting my face against you for evil, even to cut off all Judah,
44.12: and I have taken the remnant of Judah, who have set their faces to enter the land of Egypt to sojourn there, and they have all been consumed in the land of Egypt; they fall by sword, by famine they are consumed, from the least even to the greatest, by sword and by famine they die, and they have been for an execration, for an astonishment, and for a reviling, and for a reproach.
44.13: `And I have seen after those dwelling in the land of Egypt, as I saw after Jerusalem, with sword, with famine, and with pestilence,
44.14: and there is not an escaped and remaining one of the remnant of Judah, who are entering into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, even to turn back to the land of Judah, where they are lifting up their soul to return to dwell, for they do not turn back, except those escaping.'
44.15: And they answer Jeremiah--all the men who are knowing that their wives are making perfume to other gods, and all the women who are remaining, a great assembly, even all the people who are dwelling in the land of Egypt, in Pathros--saying:
44.16: `The word that you have spoken to us in the name of Jehovah--we are not hearkening to you;
44.17: for we certainly do everything that has gone out of our mouth, to make perfume to the queen of the heavens, and to pour out to her libations, as we have done, we, and our fathers, our kings, and our heads, in cities of Judah, and in streets of Jerusalem, and--we are satisfied with bread, and we are well, and evil we have not seen.
44.18: `And from the time we have ceased to make perfume to the queen of the heavens, and to pour out to her libations, we have lacked all, and by sword and by famine we have been consumed,
44.19: and when we are making perfume to the queen of the heavens, and pouring out to her libations--without our husbands have we made for her cakes to idolize her, and to pour out to her libations?'
44.20: And Jeremiah says to all the people, concerning the men and concerning the women, and concerning all the people who are answering him, saying:
44.21: `The perfume that you made in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, you, and your fathers, your kings, and your heads, and the people of the land, has not Jehovah remembered it? yes, it comes up on His heart.
44.22: And Jehovah is not able any more to accept you, because of the evil of your doings, because of the abominations that you have done, and your land is for a waste, and for an astonishment, and for a reviling, without inhabitant, as at this day.
44.23: `Because that you have made perfume, and because you have sinned against Jehovah, and have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, and in His law, and in His statutes, and in His testimonies you have not walked, therefore has this evil met you as at this day.'
44.24: And Jeremiah says to all the people, and to all the women, `Hear you a word of Jehovah, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt,
44.25: Thus spoke Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, saying: You and your wives both speak with your mouth, and with your hands have fulfilled, saying: We certainly execute our vows that we have vowed, to make perfume to the queen of the heavens, and to pour out to her libations, you do certainly establish your vows, and certainly execute your vows.
44.26: `Therefore, hear you a word of Jehovah, all Judah who are dwelling in the land of Egypt: Indeed, I--I have sworn by My great name, said Jehovah, My name is no more proclaimed by the mouth of any man of Judah, saying, Live does the Lord Jehovah--in all the land of Egypt.
44.27: Indeed, I am watching over them for evil, and not for good, and consumed have been all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt, by sword and by famine, till their consumption.
44.28: `And the escaped of the sword turn back out of the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number, and known have all the remnant of Judah who are coming into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, whose word is established, My or theirs.
44.29: `And this is to you the sign--an affirmation of Jehovah--that I am seeing after you in this place, so that you know that My words are certainly established against you for evil;
44.30: Thus said Jehovah, Indeed, I am giving Pharaoh-Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of those seeking his life, as I have given Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and who is seeking his life.'

45.1: The word that Jeremiah the prophet has spoken to Baruch son of Neriah, in his writing these words on a book from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, saying:
45.2: `Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, concerning you, O Baruch:
45.3: `You have said, Woe to me, now, for Jehovah has added sorrow to my pain, I have been wearied with my sighing, and rest I have not found.
45.4: Thus do you say to him: Thus said Jehovah: Indeed, that which I have built I am throwing down, and that which I have planted I am plucking up, even the whole land itself.
45.5: And you--you seek for you great things--do not seek, for indeed, I am bringing in evil on all flesh--an affirmation of Jehovah--and I have given to you your life for a spoil, in all places where you go.'

46.1: That which has been the word of Jehovah to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations,
46.2: For Egypt, concerning the force of Pharaoh-Necho king of Egypt, that has been by the river Phrat, in Carchemish, that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon has smitten, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:
46.3: `Set you in array shield and buckler, And draw nigh to battle.
46.4: Gird the horses, and go up, you horsemen, And station yourselves with helmets, Polish the javelins, put on the coats of mail.
46.5: Wherefore have I seen them dismayed--They are turned backward, And their mighty ones are beaten down, And to a refuge they have fled, and not turned the face? Fear is round about--an affirmation of Jehovah.
46.6: The swift do not flee, nor do the mighty escape, Northward, by the side of the river Phrat, They have stumbled and fallen.
46.7: Who is this? as a flood he comes up, As rivers do his waters shake themselves!
46.8: Egypt, as a flood comes up, And as rivers the waters shake themselves. And he says, I go up; I cover the land, I destroy the city and the inhabitants in it.
46.9: Go up, you horses; and boast yourselves, you chariots, And go forth, you mighty, Cush and Phut handling the shield, And Lud handling--treading the bow.
46.10: And that day is to the Lord Jehovah of Hosts A day of vengeance, To be avenged of His adversaries, And the sword has devoured, and been satisfied, And it has been watered from their blood, For a sacrifice is to the Lord Jehovah of Hosts, In the land of the north, by the river Phrat.
46.11: Go up to Gilead, and take balm, O virgin daughter of Egypt, In vain you have multiplied medicines, Healing there is none for you.
46.12: Nations have heard of your shame, And your cry has filled the land, For the mighty on the mighty did stumble, Together they have fallen--both of them!'
46.13: The word that Jehovah has spoken to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the coming in of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, to smite the land of Egypt:
46.14: `Declare you in Egypt, and sound in Migdol, Yes, sound in Noph, and in Tahpanhes say: Station yourself, yes, prepare for you, For a sword has devoured around you,
46.15: Wherefore has your bull been swept away? He has not stood, because Jehovah thrust him away.
46.16: He has multiplied the stumbling, Yes one has fallen upon his neighbour, And they say: Rise, and we turn back to our people, And to the land of our birth, Because of the oppressing sword.
46.17: They have cried there: Pharaoh king of Egypt is a desolation, Passed by has the appointed time.
46.18: I live--an affirmation of the King, Jehovah of Hosts is His name, Surely as Tabor is among mountains, And as Carmel by the sea--he comes in,
46.19: Goods for removal make for you, O inhabitant, daughter of Egypt, For Noph becomes a desolation, And has been burnt up, without inhabitant.
46.20: A heifer very fair is Egypt, Rending from the north does come into her.
46.21: Even her hired ones in her midst are as calves of the stall, For even they have turned, They have fled together, they have not stood, For the day of their calamity has come on them, The time of their inspection.
46.22: Its voice as a serpent goes on, For with a force they go, And with axes they have come in to her, As hewers of trees.
46.23: They have cut down her forest, An affirmation of Jehovah--for it is not searched, For they have been more than the grasshopper, And they have no numbering.
46.24: Ashamed has been the daughter of Egypt, She has been given into the hand of the people of the north.
46.25: Said has Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Indeed, I am seeing after Amon of No, And after Pharaoh, and after Egypt, And after her gods, and after her kings, And after Pharaoh, and after those trusting in him,
46.26: And I have given them into the hand of those seeking their life, And into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, And into the hand of his servants, And afterwards it is inhabited, As in days of old--an affirmation of Jehovah.
46.27: And you, you do not fear, my servant Jacob, Nor are you dismayed, O Israel, For indeed, I am saving you from afar, And your seed from the land of their captivity, And Jacob has turned back, And has been at rest, and been at ease, And there is none disturbing.
46.28: You, you do not fear, My servant Jacob, An affirmation of Jehovah--for with you I am, For I make an end of all the nations Where I have driven you, And of you I do not make an end, And I have reproved you in judgment, And do not entirely acquit you!'

47.1: That which has been the word of Jehovah to Jeremiah concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh smites Gaza:
47.2: `Thus said Jehovah: Indeed, waters are coming up from the north, And have been for an overflowing stream, And they overflow the land and its fulness, The city, and the inhabitants in it, And men have cried out, And howled has every inhabitant of the land.
47.3: From the sound of the stamping of the hoofs of his mighty ones, From the rushing of his chariot, the noise of his wheels, Fathers have not turned to sons, From feebleness of hands,
47.4: Because of the day that has come to spoil all the Philistines, To cut off to Tyre and to Zidon every helping remnant. For Jehovah is spoiling the Philistines, The remnant of the isle of Caphtor.
47.5: Come has baldness to Gaza, Cut off has been Ashkelon, O remnant of their valley, Till when do you cut yourself?
47.6: Ho, sword of Jehovah, till when are you not quiet? Be removed to your sheath, rest and cease.
47.7: How shall it be quiet, And Jehovah has given a charge to it, Against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? There has He appointed it!'

48.1: Concerning Moab: `Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Woe to Nebo, for it is spoiled, Put to shame, captured has been Kiriathaim, Put to shame has been the high tower, Yes, it has been broken down.
48.2: There is no more praise of Moab, In Heshbon they devised against it evil: Come, and we cut it off from being a nation, Also, O Madmen, you are cut off, After you goes a sword.
48.3: A voice of a cry is from Horonaim, Spoiling and great destruction.
48.4: Destroyed has been Moab, Caused a cry to be heard have her little ones.
48.5: For the ascent of Luhith with weeping, Go up does weeping, For in the descent of Horonaim Adversaries a cry of desolation have heard.
48.6: Flee you, deliver yourselves, You are as a naked thing in a wilderness.
48.7: For, because of your trusting in your works, And in your treasures, even you are captured, And gone out has Chemosh in a removal, His priests and his heads together.
48.8: And come in does a spoiler to every city, And no city does escape, And perished has the valley, And destroyed been the plain, as Jehovah said.
48.9: Give wings to Moab, for she utterly goes out, And her cities are for a desolation, Without an inhabitant in them.
48.10: Cursed is he who is doing the work of Jehovah slothfully, And cursed is he Who is withholding his sword from blood.
48.11: Secure is Moab from his youth, And at rest is he for his preserved things, And he has not been emptied out from vessel to vessel, And into captivity he has not gone, Therefore has his taste remained in him, And his fragrance has not been changed.
48.12: Therefore, indeed, days are coming, An affirmation of Jehovah, And I have sent to him wanderers, And they have caused him to wander, And his vessels they empty out, And his bottles they dash in pieces.
48.13: And ashamed has been Moab because of Chemosh, As the house of Israel have been ashamed Because of Beth-El their confidence.
48.14: How do you say, We are mighty, And men of strength for battle?
48.15: Spoiled is Moab, and her cities has one gone up, And the choice of its young men Have gone down to slaughter, An affirmation of the King, Jehovah of Hosts is His name.
48.16: Near is the calamity of Moab to come, And his affliction has hasted exceedingly.
48.17: Bemoan for him, all you round about him, And all knowing his name, say you: How has it been broken, the staff of strength, The rod of beauty.
48.18: Come down from honour, sit in thirst, O inhabitant, daughter of Dibon, For a spoiler of Moab has come up to you, He has destroyed your fenced places.
48.19: On the way stand, and watch, O inhabitant of Aroer, Ask the fugitive and escaped, Say, What has happened?
48.20: Put to shame has been Moab, For it has been broken down, Howl and cry, declare you in Arnon, For spoiled is Moab,
48.21: And judgment has come in to the land of the plain--to Holon, And to Jahazah, and on Mephaath,
48.22: And on Dibon, and on Nebo, And on Beth-Diblathaim, and on Kirathaim,
48.23: And on Beth-Gamul, and on Beth-Meon,
48.24: And on Kerioth, and on Bozrah, And on all cities of the land of Moab, The far off and the near.
48.25: Cut down has been the horn of Moab, And his arm has been broken, An affirmation of Jehovah.
48.26: Declare you him drunk, For against Jehovah he made himself great And Moab has stricken in his vomit, And he has been for a derision--even he.
48.27: And was not Israel the derision to you? Among thieves was he found? For since your words concerning him, You do bemoan yourself.
48.28: Forsake cities, and dwell in a rock, You inhabitants of Moab, And be as a dove making a nest in the passages of a pit's mouth.
48.29: We have heard of the arrogance of Moab, Exceeding proud! His haughtiness, and his arrogance, And his pride, and the height of his heart,
48.30: I--I have known, an affirmation of Jehovah, His wrath, and it is not right, His devices--not right they have done.
48.31: Therefore for Moab I howl, even for Moab--all of it, I cry for men of Kir-Heres, it does mourn,
48.32: With the weeping of Jazer, I weep for you, O vine of Sibmah, Your branches have passed over a sea, To the sea of Jazer they have come, On your summer fruits, and on your harvest, A spoiler has fallen.
48.33: And removed has been joy and gladness From the fruitful field, Even from the land of Moab, And wine from wine-presses I have caused to cease, Shouting does not proceed, The shouting is no shouting!
48.34: Because of the cry of Heshbon to Elealeh, To Jahaz they have given their voice, From Zoar to Horonaim, A heifer of the third year, For even waters of Nimrim become desolations.
48.35: And I have caused to cease to Moab, An affirmation of Jehovah, Him who is offering in a high place, And him who is making perfume to his god.
48.36: Therefore my heart for Moab as pipes does sound, And my heart for men of Kir-Heres As pipes does sound, Therefore the abundance he made did perish.
48.37: For every head is bald, and every beard diminished, On all hands cuttings, and on the loins--sackcloth.
48.38: On all roofs of Moab, and in her broad-places, All of it-- is lamentation, For I have broken Moab as a vessel in which there is no pleasure, An affirmation of Jehovah.
48.39: How has it been broken down! they have howled, How has Moab turned the neck ashamed, And Moab has been for a derision. And for a terror to all round about her.
48.40: For thus said Jehovah: Indeed, as an eagle he does flee, And has spread his wings to Moab.
48.41: Captured have been the cities, And the strongholds are caught, And the heart of the mighty of Moab Has been in that day as the heart of a distressed woman.
48.42: And Moab has been destroyed from being a people, For against Jehovah he exerted himself.
48.43: Fear, and a snare, and a gin, are for you, O inhabitant of Moab--an affirmation of Jehovah,
48.44: Whoever is fleeing because of the fear falls into the snare, And whoever is coming up from the snare is captured by the gin, For I bring in to her--to Moab--The year of their inspection, An affirmation of Jehovah.
48.45: In the shadow of Heshbon stood powerless have fugitives, For fire has gone forth from Heshbon, And a flame from within Sihon, And it consumes the corner of Moab, And the crown of the sons of Shaon.
48.46: Woe to you, O Moab, Perished has the people of Chemosh, For your sons were taken with the captives, And your daughters with the captivity.
48.47: And I have turned back to the captivity of Moab, In the latter end of the days, An affirmation of Jehovah! Hitherto is the judgment of Moab.

49.1: Concerning the sons of Ammon: `Thus said Jehovah: Sons--has Israel none? heir--has he none? Wherefore has Malcam possessed Gad? And his people in its cities have dwelt?
49.2: Therefore, indeed, days are coming, An affirmation of Jehovah, And I have sounded to Rabbah of the sons of Ammon a shout of battle, And it has been for a heap--a desolation, And her daughters with fire are burnt, And Israel has succeeded its heirs, Said has Jehovah.
49.3: Howl, Heshbon, for spoiled is Ai, Cry, daughters of Rabbah, gird on sackcloth, Lament, and go to and fro by the hedges, For Malcam into captivity does go, His priests and his princes together.
49.4: What--do you boast yourself in valleys? Flowed has your valley, O backsliding daughter, Who is trusting in her treasures: Who does come in to me?
49.5: Indeed, I am bringing in upon you a fear, An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah of Hosts, From all round about you, And you have been driven out each before it, And there is no gatherer of the wandering.
49.6: And after this I turn back the captivity of the sons of Ammon, An affirmation of Jehovah.'
49.7: Concerning Edom: `Thus said Jehovah of Hosts: Is wisdom no more in Teman? Perished has counsel from the intelligent? Vanished has their wisdom?
49.8: Flee, turn, go deep to dwell, you inhabitants of Dedan, For the calamity of Esau I brought in upon him, The time I inspected him.
49.9: If gatherers have come in to you, They do not leave gleanings, If thieves in the night, They have destroyed their sufficiency!
49.10: For I--I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, And to be hidden he is not able, Spoiled is his seed, and his brethren, And his neighbours, and he is not.
49.11: Leave your orphans--I do keep alive, And your widows--on Me trust you,
49.12: For thus said Jehovah: They whose judgment is not to drink of the cup, Do certainly drink, And you are he that is entirely acquitted! You are not acquitted, for you certainly drink.
49.13: For, by Myself, I have sworn, An affirmation of Jehovah, That for a desolation, for a reproach, For a waste, and for a reviling--is Bozrah, And all her cities are for wastes age-during.
49.14: A report I have heard from Jehovah, And an ambassador among nations is sent, Gather yourselves and come in against her, And rise you for battle.
49.15: For, indeed, little I have made you among nations, Despised among men.
49.16: Your terribleness has lifted you up, The pride of your heart, O dweller in clefts of the rock, Holding the high place of the height, For you make high as an eagle your nest, From from there I bring you down, An affirmation of Jehovah.
49.17: And Edom has been for a desolation, Every passer by her is astonished, And does hiss because of all her plagues.
49.18: As the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, And its neighbours, said Jehovah, No one does dwell there, Nor sojourn in her does a son of man.
49.19: Indeed, as a lion he comes up, Because of the rising of the Jordan, To the enduring habitation, But I cause to rest, I cause him to run from off her, And who is chosen? concerning her I lay a charge, For who is like Me? and who conveneth Me? And who is this shepherd who stands before Me?
49.20: Therefore, hear you the counsel of Jehovah, That He has counselled concerning Edom, And His devices that He has devised Concerning the inhabitants of Teman: Drag them out do not little ones of the flock, Make desolate over them does he not their habitation?
49.21: From the noise of their fall has the earth shaken, The cry--at the sea of Suph is its voice heard.
49.22: Indeed, as an eagle he comes up, and flies, And he spreads his wings over Bozrah, And the heart of the mighty of Edom has been in that day, As the heart of a distressed woman!'
49.23: Concerning Damascus: Ashamed has been Hamath and Arpad, For an evil report they have heard, They have been melted, in the sea is sorrow, To be quiet it is not able.
49.24: Feeble has been Damascus, She turned to flee, and fear strengthened her, Distress and pangs have seized her, as a travailing woman.
49.25: How is it not left--the city of praise, The city of my joy!
49.26: Therefore fall do her young men in her broad places, And all the men of war are cut off in that day, An affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts.
49.27: And I have kindled a fire against the wall of Damascus, And it consumed palaces of Ben-Hadad!'
49.28: Concerning Kedar, and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor, that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon has smitten: `Thus said Jehovah: Arise you, go you up to Kedar, And spoil the sons of the east.
49.29: Their tents and their flock they do take, Their curtains, and all their vessels, And their camels, they bear away for themselves, And they called concerning them, Fear is round about.
49.30: Flee, bemoan mightily, go deep to dwell, You inhabitants of Hazor--an affirmation of Jehovah, For given counsel against you has Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, Yes, he devises against them a device.
49.31: Rise you, go up to a nation at rest, Dwelling confidently, an affirmation of Jehovah, It has no two-leaved doors nor bar, Alone they do dwell.
49.32: And their camels have been for a prey, And the multitude of their cattle for a spoil, And I have scattered them to every wind, Who cut off the corner of the beard, And from all its passages I bring in their calamity, An affirmation of Jehovah.
49.33: And Hazor has been for a habitation of dragons, A desolation--to the age, No one does dwell there, nor sojourn in it does a son of man!'
49.34: That which has been the word of Jehovah to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying:
49.35: `Thus said Jehovah of Hosts: Indeed, I am breaking the bow of Elam, The beginning of their might.
49.36: And I have brought in to Elam four winds, From the four ends of the heavens, And have scattered them to all these winds, And there is no nation where outcasts of Elam come not in.
49.37: And I have affrighted Elam before their enemies, And before those seeking their life, And I have brought in against them evil, The heat of My anger, An affirmation of Jehovah, And I have sent after them the sword, Till I have consumed them;
49.38: And I have set My throne in Elam, And I have destroyed from there King and princes--an affirmation of Jehovah.
49.39: And it has come to pass, in the latter end of the days, I turn back to the captivity of Elam, An affirmation of Jehovah!'

50.1: The word that Jehovah has spoken concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet:
50.2: `Declare you among nations, and sound, And lift up an ensign, sound, do not hide, Say you: Captured has been Babylon, Put to shame has been Bel, Broken has been Merodach, Put to shame have been her grievous things, Broken have been her idols.
50.3: For come up against her has a nation from the north, It makes her land become a desolation, And there is not an inhabitant in it. From man even to beast, They have moved, they have gone.
50.4: In those days, and at that time, An affirmation of Jehovah, Come in do sons of Israel, They and sons of Judah together, Going on and weeping they go, And Jehovah their God they seek.
50.5: To Zion they ask the way, Thitherward are their faces: Come in, and we are joined to Jehovah, A covenant age-during--not forgotten.
50.6: A perishing flock has My people been, Their shepherds have caused them to err, To the mountains causing them to go back, From mountain to hill they have gone, They have forgotten their crouching-place.
50.7: All finding them have devoured them, And their adversaries have said: We are not guilty, Because that they sinned against Jehovah, The habitation of righteousness, And the hope of their fathers--Jehovah.
50.8: Move you from the midst of Babylon, And from the land of the Chaldeans go out. And be as he-goats before a flock.
50.9: For, indeed, I am stirring up, And am causing to come up against Babylon, An assembly of great nations from a land of the north, And they have set in array against her, From from there she is captured, Its arrow--as a skilful hero--returns not empty,
50.10: And Chaldea has been for a spoil, All her spoilers are satisfied, An affirmation of Jehovah.
50.11: Because you rejoice, because you exult, O spoilers of My inheritance, Because you increase as a heifer at the tender grass, And do cry aloud as bulls,
50.12: Ashamed has been your mother greatly, Confounded has she been that bare you, Indeed, the hindermost of nations is a wilderness, A dry land, and a desert.
50.13: Because of the wrath of Jehovah it is not inhabited, And it has been a desolation--all of it. Every passer by at Babylon is astonished, And does hiss because of all her plagues.
50.14: Set yourselves in array against Babylon round about, All you treading a bow, Shoot at her, have no pity on the arrow, For against Jehovah she has sinned.
50.15: Shout against her round about, She has given forth her hand, Fallen have her foundations, Thrown down have been her walls, For it is the vengeance of Jehovah, Be avenged of her, as she did--do you to her.
50.16: Cut off the sower from Babylon, And him handling the sickle in the time of harvest, Because of the oppressing sword, Each to his people--they turn, And each to his land--they flee.
50.17: A scattered sheep is Israel, lions have driven away, At first, devour him did the king of Asshur, And now, at last, broken his bone Has Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.
50.18: Therefore thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel: Indeed, I am seeing after the king of Babylon, And after his land, As I have seen after the king of Asshur;
50.19: And I have brought back Israel to his habitation, And he has fed on Carmel, and on Bashan. And in mount Ephraim, and on Gilead is his soul satisfied.
50.20: In those days, and at that time, An affirmation of Jehovah, Sought is the iniquity of Israel, and it is not, And the sin of Judah, and it is not found, For I am propitious to those whom I leave!
50.21: Against the land of Merathaim: Go up against it, and to the inhabitants of Pekod, Waste and devote their posterity, An affirmation of Jehovah, And do according to all that I have commanded you.
50.22: A noise of battle is in the land, and of great destruction.
50.23: How has it been cut and broken, The hammer of the whole earth! How has Babylon been for a desolation among nations!
50.24: I have laid a snare for you, And also--you are captured, O Babylon, And you--you have known, You have been found, and also are caught, For against Jehovah you have stirred yourself up.
50.25: Jehovah has opened His treasury, And He brings out the weapons of His indignation, For a work is to the Lord Jehovah of Hosts, In the land of the Chaldeans.
50.26: Come you in to her from the extremity, Open you her storehouses, Raise her up as heaps, and devote her, Let her have no remnant.
50.27: Slay all her kine, they go down to slaughter, Woe is on them, for come has their day, The time of their inspection.
50.28: A voice of fugitives and escaped ones Is from the land of Babylon, To declare in Zion the vengeance of Jehovah our God, The vengeance of His temple.
50.29: Summon to Babylon archers, all treading the bow, Encamp against her round about, Let her have no escape; Recompense to her according to her work, According to all that she did--do to her, For to Jehovah she has been proud, To the Holy One of Israel.
50.30: Therefore fall do her young men in her broad places, And all her men of war are cut off in that day, An affirmation of Jehovah.
50.31: Indeed, I am against you, O pride, An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah of Hosts, For your day has come, the time of your inspection.
50.32: And stumbled has pride, And he has fallen, and has no raiser up, And I have kindled a fire in his cities, And it has devoured all round about him.
50.33: Thus said Jehovah of Hosts: Oppressed are the sons of Israel, And the sons of Judah together, And all their captors have kept hold on them, They have refused to send them away.
50.34: Their Redeemer is strong, Jehovah of Hosts is His name, He does thoroughly plead their cause, So as to cause the land to rest, And He has given trouble to the inhabitants of Babylon.
50.35: A sword is for the Chaldeans, An affirmation of Jehovah, And it is on the inhabitants of Babylon, And on her heads, and on her wise men;
50.36: A sword is on the princes, And they have become foolish; A sword is on her mighty ones, And they have been broken down;
50.37: A sword is on his horses and on his chariot, And on all the rabble who are in her midst, And they have become women; A sword is on her treasuries, And they have been spoiled;
50.38: A sword is on her waters, and they have been dried up, For it is a land of graven images, And in idols they do boast themselves.
50.39: Therefore dwell do Ziim with Iim, Yes, dwelt in her have daughters of the ostrich, And it is not inhabited any more for ever, Nor dwelt in to all generations.
50.40: As overthrown by God with Sodom, And with Gomorrah, and with its neighbours, An affirmation of Jehovah, none does dwell there, Nor sojourn in her does a son of man.
50.41: Indeed, a people has come from the north, Even a great nation, And many kings are stirred up from the sides of the earth.
50.42: Bow and halbert they seize, Cruel are they, and they have no mercy, Their voice as a sea sounds, and on horses they ride, Set in array as a man for battle, Against you, O daughter of Babylon.
50.43: Heard has the king of Babylon their report, And feeble have been his hands, Distress has seized him; pain as a travailing woman.
50.44: Indeed, as a lion he comes up, Because of the rising of the Jordan, To the enduring habitation, But I cause to rest, I cause them to run from off her. And who is chosen? on her I lay a charge, For who is like Me? And who does convene Me? And who is this shepherd who stands before Me?
50.45: Therefore, hear you the counsel of Jehovah, That He counselled concerning Babylon, And His devices that He has devised Concerning the land of the Chaldeans; Drag them out do not little ones of the flock, Does He not make desolate over them the habitation?
50.46: From the voice: Captured was Babylon, Has the earth been shaken, And a cry among nations has been heard!

51.1: Thus said Jehovah: Indeed, I am stirring up against Babylon, And the inhabitants of Leb--My withstanders, A destroying wind,
51.2: And I have sent to Babylon fanners, And they have fanned it, and they empty its land, For they have been against it, Round about--in the day of evil.
51.3: Let not the treader tread his bow, Nor lift himself up in his coat of mail, Nor have you pity on her young men, Devote you to destruction all her host.
51.4: And fallen have the wounded in the land of the Chaldeans, And the pierced-through in her streets.
51.5: For, not forsaken is Israel and Judah, By its God--by Jehovah of Hosts, For their land has been full of guilt, Against the Holy One of Israel.
51.6: Flee you from the midst of Babylon, And deliver you each his soul, Be not cut off in its iniquity, For a time of vengeance it is to Jehovah, Recompence He is rendering to her.
51.7: A golden cup is Babylon in the hand of Jehovah, Making drunk all the earth, Of its wine drunk have nations, Therefore boast themselves do nations.
51.8: Suddenly has Babylon fallen, Yes, it is broken, howl you for it, Take balm for her pain, if so be it may be healed.
51.9: We healed Babylon, and she was not healed, Forsake her, and we go, each to his land, For come to the heavens has its judgment, And it has been lifted up to the clouds.
51.10: Jehovah has brought forth our righteousnesses, Come, and we recount in Zion the work of Jehovah our God.
51.11: Cleanse you the arrows, fill the shields, Stirred up has Jehovah the spirit of the kings of Madia, For against Babylon His device is to destroy it, For the vengeance of Jehovah it is, The vengeance of His temple.
51.12: To the walls of Babylon lift up an ensign, Strengthen the watch, Establish the watchers, prepare the ambush, For Jehovah has both devised and done that which He spoke, Concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
51.13: O dweller on many waters, abundant in treasures, Come in has your end, the measure of your dishon gain.
51.14: Sworn has Jehovah of Hosts by Himself, That, Surely I have filled you with men as the cankerworm, And they have cried against you--shouting.
51.15: The maker of earth by His power, The establisher of the world by His wisdom, Who by His understanding stretched out the heavens,
51.16: At the voice He gives forth, A multitude of waters are in the heavens, And He causes vapours to come up from the end of the earth, Lightnings for rain He has made, And He brings out wind from His treasures.
51.17: Brutish has been every man by knowledge, Put to shame has been every refiner by a graven image, For false is his molten image, And there is no breath in them.
51.18: Vanity are they--work of errors, In the time of their inspection they perish.
51.19: Not like these is the portion of Jacob, For He is former of all things, And Israel is the rod of His inheritance, Jehovah of Hosts is His name.
51.20: An axe are you to me--weapons of war, And I have broken in pieces by you nations, And I have destroyed by you kingdoms,
51.21: And I have broken in pieces by you horse and its rider, And I have broken in pieces by you chariot and its charioteer,
51.22: And I have broken in pieces by you man and woman, And I have broken in pieces by you old and young, And I have broken in pieces by you young man and virgin,
51.23: And I have broken in pieces by you shepherd and his drove, And I have broken in pieces by you husbandman and his team, And I have broken in pieces by you governors and prefects.
51.24: And I have recompensed to Babylon, And to all inhabitants of Chaldea, All the evil that they have done in Zion, Before your eyes--an affirmation of Jehovah.
51.25: Indeed, I am against you, O destroying mount, An affirmation of Jehovah, That is destroying all the earth, And I have stretched out My hand against you, And I have rolled you from the rocks, And given you for a burnt mountain.
51.26: And they take not out of you a stone for a corner, And a stone for foundations, For desolations age-during are you, An affirmation of Jehovah.
51.27: Lift you up an ensign in the land, Blow a trumpet among nations, Sanctify against it nations, Summon against it the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz, Appoint against it an infant head, Cause the horse to ascend as the rough cankerworm.
51.28: Sanctify against it the nations with the kings of Media, Its governors and all its prefects, And all the land of its dominion.
51.29: And shake does the land, and it is pained, For stood against Babylon have the purposes of Jehovah, To make the land of Babylon a desolation without inhabitant.
51.30: Ceased have the mighty of Babylon to fight, They have remained in strongholds, Failed has their might, they have become woman, They have burnt her tabernacles, Broken have been her bars.
51.31: Runner to meet runner does run, And announcer to meet announcer, To announce to the king of Babylon, For, captured has been his city--at the extremity.
51.32: And the passages have been captured, And the reeds they have burnt with fire, And the men of war have been troubled.
51.33: For thus said Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, The daughter of Babylon is as a threshing-floor, The time of her threshing--yet a little, And come has the time of her harvest.
51.34: Devoured us, crushed us, has Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, He has set us as an empty vessel, He has swallowed us as a dragon, He has filled his belly with my dainties, He has driven us away.
51.35: My wrong, and that of my flesh is on Babylon, Say does the inhabitant of Zion, And my blood is on the inhabitants of Chaldea, Say does Jerusalem.
51.36: Therefore, thus said Jehovah: Indeed, I am pleading your cause, And I have avenged your vengeance, And dried up its sea, and made its fountains dry.
51.37: And Babylon has been for heaps, A habitation of dragons, An astonishment, and a hissing, without inhabitant.
51.38: Together as young lions they roar, They have shaken themselves as lions' whelps.
51.39: In their heat I make their banquets, And I have caused them to drink, so that they exult, And have slept a sleep age-during, And awake not--an affirmation of Jehovah.
51.40: I cause them to go down as lambs to slaughter, As rams with he-goats.
51.41: How has Sheshach been captured, Yes, caught is the praise of the whole earth, How has Babylon been for an astonishment among nations.
51.42: Come up against Babylon has the sea, With a multitude of its billows it has been covered.
51.43: Its cities have been for a desolation, A dry land, and a wilderness, A land--none does dwell in them, Nor pass over into them does a son of man.
51.44: And I have seen after Bel in Babylon, And I have brought forth that which he swallowed--from his mouth, And flow no more to him do nations, Also the wall of Babylon has fallen.
51.45: Go forth from its midst, O My people, And deliver you, each his soul, Because of the fierceness of the anger of Jehovah,
51.46: And lest your heart be tender, And you be afraid of the report that is heard in the land, And come in a year has the report, And after it in a year the report, And violence is in the land, ruler against ruler;
51.47: Therefore, indeed, days are coming, And I have seen after the graven images of Babylon. And all its land is ashamed, And all its pierced ones do fall in its midst.
51.48: And cried aloud against Babylon Have heavens and earth, and all that is in them, For, from the north come to it do the spoilers, An affirmation of Jehovah.
51.49: Even Babylon is to fall, you pierced of Israel, Even they of Babylon have fallen, You pierced of all the earth.
51.50: You escaped of the sword, go on, stand not, Remember you from afar Jehovah, And let Jerusalem come up on your heart.
51.51: We have been ashamed, for we heard reproach, Covered has shame our faces, For come in have strangers, against the sanctuaries of the house of Jehovah.
51.52: Therefore, indeed, days are coming, An affirmation of Jehovah, And I have seen after its graven images, And in all its land groan does the wounded.
51.53: Because Babylon goes up to the heavens, And because it fences the high place of its strength, From Me come into it do spoilers, An affirmation of Jehovah.
51.54: A voice of a cry is from Babylon, And of great destruction from the land of the Chaldean.
51.55: For Jehovah is spoiling Babylon, And has destroyed out of it a great voice, And sounded have its billows as many waters, Given forth a noise has their voice.
51.56: For come in against it--against Babylon--has a spoiler, And captured have been its mighty ones, Broken have been their bows, For the God of recompences--Jehovah--does certainly repay.
51.57: And I have caused its princes to drink, And its wise men, its governors, And its prefects, and its mighty ones, And they have slept a sleep age-during, And they awake not--an affirmation of the king, Jehovah of Hosts is His name.
51.58: Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, the wall of Babylon--The broad one--is utterly made bare, And her high gates with fire are burnt, And peoples labour in vain, And nations in fire, and have been weary!
51.59: The word that Jeremiah the prophet has commanded Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, in his going with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon, in the fourth year of his reign--and Seraiah is a quiet prince;
51.60: and Jeremiah writes all the evil that comes to Babylon on one book--all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
51.61: And Jeremiah says to Seraiah, `When you do enter Babylon, then you have seen, and have read all these words,
51.62: and have said: Jehovah, You, You have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, that there is none dwelling in it, from man even to cattle, for it is a desolation age-during.
51.63: And it has come to pass, when you do finish reading this book, you do bind to it a stone, and have cast it into the midst of Phrat,
51.64: and said, Thus sink does Babylon, and it does not arise, because of the evil that I am bringing in against it, and they have been weary.' Hitherto are words of Jeremiah.

52.1: A son of twenty and one years is Zedekiah in his reigning, and eleven years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
52.2: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, according to all that Jehoiakim has done,
52.3: for, because of the anger of Jehovah, it has been in Jerusalem and Judah till He has cast them from before His face, and Zedekiah does rebel against the king of Babylon.
52.4: And it comes to pass, in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth of the month, come has Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon--he and all his force--against Jerusalem, and they encamp against it, and build against it a fortification round about;
52.5: and the city comes into siege till the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
52.6: In the fourth month, in the ninth of the month, when the famine is severe in the city, and there has been no bread for the people of the land,
52.7: then is the city broken up, and all the men of war flee, and go forth from the city by night, the way of the gate between the two walls, that is by the king's garden--and the Chaldeans are by the city round about--and they go the way of the plain.
52.8: And the forces of the Chaldeans pursue after the king, and overtake Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his forces have been scattered from him,
52.9: and they capture the king, and bring him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah, in the land of Hamath, and he speaks with him--judgments.
52.10: And the king of Babylon slaughters the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and also all the princes of Judah has he slaughtered in Riblah;
52.11: and the eyes of Zedekiah he has blinded, and he binds him in brazen fetters, and the king of Babylon brings him to Babylon, and puts him in the house of inspection to the day of his death.
52.12: And in the fifth month, in the tenth of the month--it is the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon--come has Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners; he has stood before the king of Babylon in Jerusalem,
52.13: and he burns the house of Jehovah, and the house of the king, and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every great house he has burned with fire,
52.14: and all the walls of Jerusalem round about broken down have all the forces of the Chaldeans that are with the chief of the executioners.
52.15: And of the poor of the people, and the remnant of the people who are left in the city, and those who are falling away, who have fallen to the king of Babylon, and the remnant of the multitude, has Nebuzar-Adan chief of the executioners, removed;
52.16: and of the poor of the land has Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, left for vine-dressers and for husbandmen.
52.17: And the pillars of brass that are to the house of Jehovah, and the bases, and the brasen sea that is in the house of Jehovah, have the Chaldeans broken, and they bear away all the brass of them to Babylon;
52.18: and the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the bowls, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass with which they minister, they have taken away;
52.19: and the basins, and the fire-pans, and the bowls, and the pots, and the candlesticks, and the spoons, and the cups, the gold of that which is gold, and the silver of that which is silver, has the chief of the executioners taken.
52.20: The two pillars, the one sea, and the twelve brazen oxen that are beneath the bases, that king Solomon made for the house of Jehovah, there was no weighing of the brass of all these vessels.
52.21: As to the pillars, eighteen cubits is the height of the one pillar, and a cord of twelve cubits does compass it, and its thickness is four fingers hollow.
52.22: And the chapiter upon it is of brass, and the height of the one chapiter is five cubits, and net-work and pomegranates are on the chapiter round about, the whole is of brass; and like these have the second pillar, and pomegranates.
52.23: And the pomegranates are ninety and six on a side, all the pomegranates are a hundred on the net-work round about.
52.24: And the chief of the executioners takes Seraiah the head priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold,
52.25: and out of the city he has taken a certain eunuch, who has been inspector over the men of war, and seven men of those seeing the king's face, who have been found in the city, and the head scribe of the host, who musters the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land, who are found in the midst of the city;
52.26: and Nebuzar-Adan, chief of the executioners, takes them, and brings them to the king of Babylon to Riblah,
52.27: and the king of Babylon smites them, and puts them to death in Riblah, in the land of Hamath, and he removes Judah from off its own ground.
52.28: This is the people whom Nebuchadrezzar has removed: in the seventh year, of Jews, three thousand and twenty and three;
52.29: in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar--from Jerusalem, souls, eight hundred thirty and two;
52.30: in the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar, has Nebuzar-Adan chief of the guard removed of Jewish souls, seven hundred forty and five; all the souls are four thousand and six hundred.
52.31: And it comes to pass, in the thirty and seventh year of the removal of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the twenty and fifth of the month, has Evil-Merodach king of Babylon lifted up, in the year of his reign, the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brings him out from the house of restraint,
52.32: and speaks with him good things, and sets his throne above the throne of the kings who are with him in Babylon,
52.33: and he has changed his prison garments, and he has eaten bread before him continually, all the days of his life.
52.34: And his allowance--a continual allowance--has been given to him by the king of Babylon, the matter of a day in its day, till the day of his death--all days of his life.
